patterns-of-inheritance.scope: Autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, X-linked recessive, X-linked dominant, mitochondrial inheritance, variable expressivity, incomplete penetrance, germline mosaicism
patterns-of-inheritance.core: Pedigree patterns reflect allele location and dominance; recurrence risk depends on parental genotype, penetrance, and whether the variant is inherited or new.

rows.label: Definition
items: ★ **Incomplete penetrance**: some variant carriers never develop phenotype
★ **Variable expressivity**: affected carriers differ in severity or manifestations
Germline mosaicism: pathogenic variant in some parental gametes despite negative blood testing

rows.label: Interpret
items: Vertical pattern → consider dominant; affected siblings with unaffected parents → recessive
★ **Male-to-male transmission excludes X-linked inheritance**
Consanguinity increases recessive risk; recurrence probability resets each pregnancy

rows.label: Use when
items: Family counseling, genetic testing, recurrence prediction, carrier identification

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Apparent de novo disease can recur in siblings through **parental germline mosaicism**
Mitochondrial heteroplasmy/threshold effects cause variable severity; not every child is equally affected
Small pedigrees, reduced penetrance, new variants, or skewed X-inactivation can obscure classic patterns

table.title: Recurrence: other parent noncarrier unless stated
rows: 50% inherit variant; phenotype depends on penetrance
All daughters inherit; no sons inherit
Maternal transmission possible; paternal transmission absent

patterns-of-inheritance.evidence: Definitions and Mendelian probabilities; no clinical guideline involved.

postoperative-fever.name: Postoperative fever
postoperative-fever.scope: Timing (Wind, Water, Wound, Walking, Wonder drugs), atelectasis, surgical site infection, intra-abdominal abscess
postoperative-fever.core: Fever after surgery: postoperative interval narrows causes; hemodynamic instability or focal findings determine urgency, testing, and source control.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Emergency or contaminated surgery, bowel anastomosis, diabetes, immunosuppression
Prolonged ventilation, urinary catheters, central lines, immobility; new medications or transfusion

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Shock, rapidly spreading wound pain, crepitus** → invasive infection regardless of postoperative day
Purulent drainage, dysuria, productive cough, hypoxemia, or abdominal tenderness localize the source
Persistent ileus, leukocytosis, recurrent fever after initial improvement → intra-abdominal collection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammatory cytokines arise from sterile injury or infection; later onset raises infection probability
**Atelectasis does not establish the cause of fever**; historical Wind attribution lacks supporting evidence

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Examine first**: incision, lungs, abdomen, lines, urine symptoms, legs; timing alone never diagnoses
Stable isolated fever within 48 hours → observation; avoid reflex cultures or antibiotics
Focal findings → chest radiograph, urinalysis/culture, or wound culture; sepsis → blood cultures and lactate
★ Suspected deep abdominal infection → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**

rows.label: Tx
items: Sepsis → IV crystalloids, broad antibiotics, urgent source control; do not delay for imaging
Superficial incisional abscess → open/drain; add antibiotics for cellulitis or systemic illness
★ Intra-abdominal abscess → **percutaneous drainage + piperacillin-tazobactam**; anastomotic leak/peritonitis → surgery
Pulmonary collapse → analgesia, mobilization, lung expansion; suspected drug fever → stop culprit

rows.label: Complications
items: Septic shock, dehiscence, organ failure; missed anastomotic leak → diffuse peritonitis
Unnecessary antimicrobials → C difficile, resistance; immobilization → VTE

rows.label: Prevention
items: Preincision antibiotic prophylaxis, aseptic technique, glucose control; promptly remove unnecessary catheters
Early ambulation, pulmonary hygiene, mechanical/pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis when bleeding risk permits

rows.label: Mimics
items: Malignant hyperthermia: perioperative rigidity, rapidly rising end-tidal CO2, hyperthermia
Transfusion reaction: fever temporally linked to blood administration; stop transfusion immediately

table.title: Timing: clues, not diagnostic rules
rows: Sterile inflammation; aspiration; dangerous early wound infection
Walking: VTE; Wonder drugs: drug fever

postoperative-fever.evidence: Atelectasis evidence checked 2026-10-30: [Chest systematic review, 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21527508/); remaining management: established surgical teaching.

postpartum-care.name: Postpartum care
postpartum-care.scope: Normal puerperal changes, lochia, uterine involution, perineal and cesarean wound healing, breastfeeding, postpartum depression screening, routine postpartum visit
postpartum-care.core: Postpartum care is an ongoing assessment of recovery, mood, infant feeding, contraception, and chronic disease after every birth.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ All postpartum patients; assess support, sleep, safety, sexual health, and reproductive goals

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Contact within **3 weeks**; comprehensive visit by **12 weeks**, with earlier risk-based review
Hypertensive disorder → BP within 7–10 days; severe hypertension → within 72 hours

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Edinburgh or PHQ-9 depression screen; assess suicidality directly after positive self-harm response
BP, bleeding, fundal tenderness; inspect perineum/incision for erythema, drainage, separation
Observe latch/milk transfer; frequent feeds, lactation support; cracked nipples → correct positioning

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Heavy bleeding, fever, dyspnea, severe headache → urgent evaluation
Mood screen positive → diagnostic interview, psychotherapy/SSRI; psychosis → emergency hospitalization
Increasing wound pain/purulence → evaluate infection; breast fluctuance → ultrasound for abscess

rows.label: Traps
items: Ovulation may precede first period; discuss contraception before discharge
Lactational contraception: amenorrhea, exclusive frequent breastfeeding, infant <6 months
Postpartum hypertension and cardiomyopathy can first appear after discharge

table.title: Expected recovery
rows: Descends daily; near prepregnancy size by 6 weeks
Pain progressively improves; keep clean, monitor healing
Early cramping and fluid loss; breastfeeding intensifies cramping

postpartum-care.evidence: Visit timing checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG postpartum care](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/05/optimizing-postpartum-care); normal physiology established teaching.

preterm-labor.name: Preterm labor
preterm-labor.scope: Preterm labor (<37 weeks), cervical insufficiency, tocolysis (indomethacin, nifedipine), antenatal corticosteroids (betamethasone), magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection, GBS chemoprophylaxis
preterm-labor.core: Regular contractions with cervical change before 37 weeks; briefly delay eligible early births to improve neonatal outcomes, without prolonging unsafe pregnancies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior spontaneous preterm birth, short cervix, multiple gestation, infection, smoking, uterine anomalies
Cervical surgery or prior painless second-trimester loss suggests cervical insufficiency

rows.label: Clues
items: Pelvic pressure, backache, increased discharge, contractions; assess membrane rupture and bleeding
Fever, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia → intraamniotic infection; maternal/fetal instability changes delivery timing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature inflammatory/uterine activation versus mechanically weak cervix with painless dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Sterile speculum examination** for pooling and cervix; ultrasound dates pregnancy and assesses presentation
Transvaginal cervical length; selected symptomatic cases: negative fetal fibronectin predicts low imminent birth risk
Collect GBS culture, urine studies; exclude previa before digital examination with bleeding

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Birth within 7 days, **24–33 6/7 weeks** → betamethasone; selected untreated 34–36 6/7-week pregnancies also eligible
★ Delivery expected <32 weeks → **magnesium sulfate** for neuroprotection, not primary tocolysis
Tocolysis: 48 hours for steroids/transfer; no maintenance; late-preterm steroids avoided with pregestational diabetes
★ **No tocolysis** with infection, significant abruption, severe preeclampsia, or fetal compromise; proceed toward delivery
Intrapartum penicillin for positive/unknown GBS; no routine antibiotics for intact membranes without infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Neonatal RDS, IVH, NEC, sepsis, cerebral palsy; magnesium toxicity → hyporeflexia, respiratory depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Singleton short cervix ≤20 mm before 24 weeks → vaginal progesterone; consider at 21–25 mm
Cervical insufficiency/prior qualifying loss → cerclage; selected prior preterm birth plus short cervix also eligible
17-hydroxyprogesterone caproate no longer recommended; progesterone without short cervix does not prevent recurrence

rows.label: Mimics
items: Braxton Hicks: no progressive dilation
Cervical insufficiency: painless dilation, minimal contractions
PPROM: membrane rupture precedes labor; distinct latency-antibiotic pathway

pubertal-development.name: Pubertal development
pubertal-development.scope: Tanner stages, normal thelarche vs breast mass, premature adrenarche, precocious puberty, constitutional delay of growth and puberty
pubertal-development.core: Interpret sexual maturation by sequence, age, growth velocity, and bone age; isolated benign variants lack progressive gonadal activation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Constitutional delay often familial; chronic illness, undernutrition, excess exercise delay maturation
CNS lesions, gonadal/adrenal hormone excess, exogenous sex steroids can cause early puberty

rows.label: Clues
items: Girls: breast budding precedes peak growth, then menarche about 2–3 years later
Boys: testes enlarge before penile growth; pubic hair reflects adrenarche, not necessarily gonadarche
★ Asymmetric tender **subareolar breast bud** at expected age usually normal; hard eccentric mass needs evaluation
Rapid height acceleration, advancing secondary characteristics, neurologic symptoms → pathologic early maturation concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Central puberty: hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility → LH/FSH → gonadal steroids
Adrenarche produces adrenal androgens independently; peripheral hormone excess suppresses pituitary gonadotropins

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Precocious: secondary sexual development **before 8 years girls or 9 years boys**
★ Delayed: **no breasts by 13**, no testes ≥4 mL by 14; evaluate absent menarche by 15
Growth chart, Tanner examination, bone age; LH/FSH, estradiol/testosterone, TSH selected by pattern
Central precocity → pubertal basal/stimulated LH; brain MRI especially boys, young girls, neurologic signs
Peripheral pattern → targeted adrenal/gonadal tests/imaging; isolated adrenarche requires exclusion of rapid virilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Progressive central precocity → **GnRH agonist**; treat CNS cause when present
Peripheral precocity → remove hormone source or treat tumor/adrenal disorder; GnRH agonist alone ineffective
Constitutional delay → reassurance, follow growth; distress → specialist-guided brief sex-steroid course
Benign premature thelarche/adrenarche → observe progression; no automatic hormonal treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Early epiphyseal closure → reduced adult height; psychosocial distress
Missed hypogonadism → impaired bone accrual; untreated CNS/tumor cause may progress

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, manage chronic disease, avoid household hormone exposure; serial growth surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Primary gonadal failure: high LH/FSH, low sex steroids
Permanent central hypogonadism: absent progression rather than eventual familial catch-up

pubertal-development.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric endocrine timing and Tanner staging.

recurrent-pregnancy-loss.name: Recurrent pregnancy loss
recurrent-pregnancy-loss.scope: Definition (two or more losses), antiphospholipid syndrome, congenital uterine anomalies (septate, bicornuate), parental chromosomal translocations, endocrine causes, diagnostic workup
recurrent-pregnancy-loss.core: Two or more spontaneous pregnancy losses warrant evaluation; ASRM 2026 includes hCG-confirmed biochemical losses and excludes confirmed ectopic or molar pregnancies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal age/aneuploidy, parental rearrangements, APS, uterine anomalies, uncontrolled diabetes/hypothyroidism
Smoking, obesity; many recurrent losses remain unexplained despite evaluation

rows.label: Clues
items: Repeated early loss favors chromosomal causes; later loss may suggest anatomy or placental disease
Prior thrombosis, fetal death ≥10 weeks, or early severe preeclampsia raises APS suspicion
Painless second-trimester dilation suggests cervical insufficiency rather than a primary endocrine cause

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Embryonic genetic imbalance, abnormal uterine cavity, or placental thromboinflammation disrupts successful gestation
Septum has abnormal implantation environment; balanced carriers can produce unbalanced embryos

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Miscarriage-tissue chromosomal microarray** when feasible; result guides further evaluation
★ **Uterine cavity assessment**: saline sonography, HSG, or hysteroscopy; 3D ultrasound distinguishes external contour
Parental karyotypes if unbalanced rearrangement found or tissue testing unavailable; offer genetic counseling
APS clinical criteria → lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, anti-β2-glycoprotein I; repeat positives ≥12 weeks later
TSH for symptoms/risk or unexplained/euploid losses; HbA1c with diabetes risks; prolactin only with suggestive symptoms

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Confirmed obstetric APS → **aspirin + heparin**; treat overt thyroid disease and uncontrolled diabetes
Septum/cavity lesion → discuss hysteroscopic correction; live-birth benefit uncertain
Translocation → reproductive genetic counseling, expectant conception or IVF with targeted genetic testing
★ Unexplained loss → support and expectant care; **no empiric anticoagulation**
Vaginal progesterone may be offered with early bleeding/prior recurrent loss after discussing uncertain benefit

rows.label: Complications
items: Grief, anxiety/depression; repeated uterine instrumentation → adhesions; treatment burden and financial stress

rows.label: Prevention
items: Preconception folic acid, smoking cessation, metabolic optimization; early supportive follow-up in next pregnancy
Avoid routine inherited thrombophilia, NK-cell, infectious panels, or ovarian-reserve tests without separate indications

rows.label: Mimics
items: Infertility: failure to achieve pregnancy rather than loss after conception
Sporadic miscarriage: common isolated aneuploid event, no recurrent-loss workup after one uncomplicated loss

recurrent-pregnancy-loss.evidence: Updated workup checked 2026-10-30: [ASRM 2026](https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/recurrent-pregnancy-loss-a-committee-opinion-2026/); anatomy established teaching.

rh-alloimmunization.name: Rh alloimmunization
rh-alloimmunization.scope: Rh(D) and other red cell alloimmunization (Kell, Duffy), anti-D immune globulin prophylaxis, indirect Coombs titer monitoring, fetomaternal hemorrhage (Kleihauer-Betke), middle cerebral artery Doppler for fetal anemia
rh-alloimmunization.core: Maternal IgG against fetal red-cell antigens crosses the placenta, causing fetal anemia, hydrops, and neonatal hemolysis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Antigen-negative mother/positive fetus; prior pregnancy, transfusion, bleeding, trauma, invasive procedures
Anti-D, anti-Kell, and anti-Duffy clinically significant; ABO incompatibility usually milder

rows.label: Clues
items: Often asymptomatic mother; fetal ascites, skin edema, placentomegaly, cardiomegaly
Neonate: early jaundice, pallor, reticulocytosis; severe disease → cardiovascular collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: First exposure sensitizes; subsequent antigen exposure produces an anamnestic response
Kell antibodies additionally suppress erythropoiesis; low titers can still cause severe disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First prenatal visit: ABO/Rh type + **indirect Coombs**; repeat before routine antenatal prophylaxis
Identify antibody → fetal antigen status, serial titers; neonatal **direct Coombs** detects RBC-bound antibodies
★ Critical titer, often **1:16**, or previously affected pregnancy → middle cerebral artery Doppler
MCA peak systolic velocity >1.5 MoM → fetal blood sampling; Kell warrants specialist surveillance
Kleihauer-Betke quantifies hemorrhage for dosing: **300 µg covers 30 mL fetal whole blood**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe preterm fetal anemia → **intrauterine transfusion**; near term → delivery
Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia → phototherapy; severe hemolysis → exchange transfusion

rows.label: Complications
items: High-output heart failure, stillbirth, bilirubin encephalopathy, delayed neonatal anemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Unsensitized Rh-negative mother: **anti-D immune globulin** at 28 weeks and within 72 hours postpartum
Postpartum prophylaxis only with Rh-positive/unknown infant; also after sensitizing events; adjust dose for hemorrhage
★ Established anti-D sensitization → prophylaxis ineffective; no equivalent prophylaxis for Kell/Duffy
ACOG 2024: routine Rh testing/prophylaxis may be forgone for abortion/loss before 12 weeks

rows.label: Mimics
items: Parvovirus: nonimmune hydrops with negative maternal antibody screen
ABO hemolysis: may affect first pregnancy; fetal hydrops uncommon

rh-alloimmunization.evidence: Prophylaxis checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG Rh guidance](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/the-rh-factor-how-it-can-affect-your-pregnancy), [2024 update](https://doi.org/10.1097/AOG.0000000000005733); remaining content established teaching.

routine-prenatal-care.name: Routine prenatal care and early pregnancy
routine-prenatal-care.scope: Pregnancy diagnosis (beta-hCG), initial prenatal assessment, routine first-trimester screening, aneuploidy screening
routine-prenatal-care.core: Confirm and date pregnancy, assess maternal risks, offer one aneuploidy-screening strategy or diagnostic testing, and arrange time-sensitive prenatal studies.

rows.label: Who
items: All pregnancies; review obstetric history, drugs, illness, substance use, violence, family history
Offer carrier screening and genetic counseling; discuss patient preferences and right to decline

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Early visit: urine hCG confirms pregnancy; serum quantitative hCG for uncertain/complicated cases
★ First-trimester **ultrasound crown–rump length** best establishes gestational age
Serum screen 10–13 6/7 weeks; NT 11–13 6/7; cfDNA from 10 weeks

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Initial **CBC, ABO/Rh, antibody screen, urine culture**; HIV, syphilis, HBsAg, HCV, rubella immunity
GC/chlamydia by age/risk; offer one aneuploidy strategy regardless of maternal age
Anatomy ultrasound 18–22 weeks; AFP for open neural tube defects when not otherwise assessed

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Abnormal screen → counseling, ultrasound, **CVS/amniocentesis** before irreversible decisions
CVS: 10–13 weeks; amniocentesis: ≥15 weeks; neither automatically required after negative screening
Rh-negative, unsensitized → anti-D prophylaxis at 28 weeks and after sensitizing events

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **cfDNA is screening**, not diagnostic; does not screen open neural tube defects
Single hCG value cannot establish viability or location; pain/bleeding → ectopic evaluation
Folate before conception/early gestation; avoid alcohol, tobacco, teratogens; no live vaccines

toxic-shock-syndrome.name: Toxic shock syndrome
toxic-shock-syndrome.core: Abrupt fever, hypotension and multiorgan dysfunction from toxin-producing staphylococci or streptococci; remove the source, resuscitate, and suppress toxin production immediately.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Retained tampon, nasal packing, postoperative wound, burns, postpartum infection; no foreign body required
GAS invasive soft-tissue infection, skin break or recent varicella; diabetes and immunosuppression increase severity

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Diffuse erythroderma + shock**, vomiting/diarrhea, myalgias, mucosal hyperemia suggest staphylococcal disease
Palmar/plantar desquamation typically delayed 1–2 weeks; its absence early cannot exclude diagnosis
★ **Severe focal pain out of proportion**, rapid tissue progression → streptococcal necrotizing infection
Renal/hepatic injury, thrombocytopenia, confusion, hypoxemia; rash less consistent with streptococcal disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Superantigens activate T cells outside normal antigen specificity → massive cytokine release, capillary leak
Staphylococcal disease often toxin-mediated from local colonization; GAS usually invasive with bacteremia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; CBC, metabolic/liver tests, lactate, coagulation studies assess organ injury
Blood cultures + source/wound cultures before antibiotics if no meaningful delay
Staphylococcal blood cultures often negative; GAS blood/tissue cultures frequently positive
Concern for necrotizing fasciitis → surgical exploration; CT must not delay debridement

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV crystalloids, norepinephrine**, ICU support; remove tampon/packing, drain abscesses, debride infected tissue
Empiric **vancomycin + clindamycin**; add piperacillin-tazobactam if polymicrobial deep infection possible
★ Confirmed GAS → **penicillin G + clindamycin**; clindamycin suppresses toxin synthesis
Confirmed MSSA → nafcillin/oxacillin or cefazolin plus initial toxin suppression; MRSA → continue vancomycin
Refractory severe streptococcal shock → consider IVIG with specialists; survival benefit uncertain

rows.label: Complications
items: DIC, ARDS, acute kidney injury, cardiomyopathy, limb loss, death
Staphylococcal recurrence possible because protective immunity may be incomplete

rows.label: Prevention
items: Use lowest-absorbency tampon, change regularly; avoid prolonged intravaginal retention and retained surgical packing
After menstrual TSS, counsel alternative menstrual products; meticulous wound care and prompt infection treatment
Routine household antibiotic prophylaxis for invasive GAS generally unnecessary; public-health exceptions depend on risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic shock: similar physiology without characteristic toxin-associated rash or source
Meningococcemia: petechiae/purpura, meningitis, positive blood cultures
Kawasaki disease: prolonged pediatric fever and mucocutaneous findings; coronary disease, usually no shock

toxic-shock-syndrome.evidence: GAS management checked 2026-10-30: [CDC streptococcal TSS guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/group-a-strep/hcp/clinical-guidance/streptococcal-toxic-shock-syndrome.html); staphylococcal management: established infectious-disease teaching.

urinary-incontinence.name: Urinary incontinence
urinary-incontinence.core: Involuntary urine leakage is classified by triggers, urgency, bladder emptying, and ability to reach a toilet; reversible contributors often coexist.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childbirth, pelvic surgery, aging, obesity; diabetes, neurologic disease, prostate enlargement
Diuretics, sedatives, anticholinergics, constipation, infection, impaired mobility/cognition worsen control

rows.label: Clues
items: History: timing, volume, dysuria, weak stream, nocturia, fluid intake, obstetric/surgical and neurologic history
★ **New saddle anesthesia, leg weakness, retention** → urgent cauda equina evaluation
Continuous leakage after pelvic surgery suggests fistula; recurrent UTIs/hematuria require further investigation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Urethral support/sphincter failure, involuntary detrusor contraction, or impaired emptying produce distinct leakage patterns
Functional impairment can prevent continence despite intact lower urinary tract function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis + voiding diary**, focused pelvic/prostate and neurologic examination; review medications
Cough stress test with reasonably full bladder; assess prolapse, atrophy, fecal impaction
★ Suspected retention/emptying symptoms → **postvoid residual**; persistent >200 mL suggests inadequate emptying
No routine initial urodynamics/cystoscopy; uncertainty, hematuria, refractory symptoms → additional testing

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat reversible contributor; mixed incontinence → target most bothersome component
★ **Pelvic floor training/bladder training** underpin conservative care; weight loss, reduce caffeine, timed voiding
Urgency drugs: mirabegron or antimuscarinic; discuss cognitive risk and avoid antimuscarinics with retention
Mirabegron may increase BP; avoid severe uncontrolled hypertension; refractory urgency → botulinum toxin or neuromodulation
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause → local vaginal estrogen when suitable; not systemic estrogen for leakage

rows.label: Complications
items: Dermatitis, falls from rushing, social isolation, sleep disruption
Overflow → hydronephrosis/renal injury; bladder botulinum toxin → retention, UTI

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication review, accessible toilet, mobility aids; bowel regularity, maintain strength and weight

rows.label: Mimics
items: Polyuria: high urine volume from hyperglycemia/diuresis rather than primary storage failure
Vaginal fistula: constant leakage unrelated to voiding urge or exertion

urinary-tract-infections.name: Urinary tract infections
urinary-tract-infections.scope: Asymptomatic bacteriuria, acute cystitis, pyelonephritis, catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI), catheter removal, empiric antibiotics
urinary-tract-infections.core: Symptoms localize urinary infection: bladder disease lacks systemic illness; renal involvement causes fever or flank pain; bacteriuria alone is insufficient.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual activity, spermicides, pregnancy, obstruction/stones, urinary retention, instrumentation
Catheter duration, diabetes, prior resistant isolates or antibiotics increase complicated-course risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic discomfort; absent vaginal discharge supports urinary source
★ **Rigors, CVA tenderness, vomiting, hypotension** → pyelonephritis or urosepsis
Catheterized patients: new urinary/systemic symptoms; cloudy urine or pyuria alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Usually ascending enteric bacteria, predominantly E coli; catheter biofilm maintains colonization
Urease-producing Proteus alkalinizes urine → struvite calculi and persistent infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**: pyuria, leukocyte esterase, nitrites; negative nitrites do not exclude infection
Culture: pyelonephritis, pregnancy, CAUTI, recurrence/resistance; classic cystitis often clinical
Persistent fever after 48–72 hours, sepsis, or suspected obstruction → renal imaging
Asymptomatic bacteriuria: usually ≥100,000 CFU/mL; delirium alone → seek other causes without automatic antibiotics

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Treat asymptomatic bacteriuria only in pregnancy or before urologic mucosal trauma** in routine adult scenarios
★ CAUTI → **remove unnecessary catheter**; if needed and present >2 weeks, replace before culture/treatment
★ Infected obstructed collecting system → **urgent drainage + IV antibiotics**; antibiotics alone insufficient
Improving nonpregnant pyelonephritis: fluoroquinolone 5–7 days, other active drugs 7 days; high-risk cases individualized

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacteremia, septic shock, renal/perinephric abscess; pregnancy → preterm birth
Antibiotics → resistance, C difficile; fluoroquinolones → tendon injury, QT prolongation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid unnecessary catheters; closed drainage, daily removal assessment
Postmenopausal recurrence → vaginal estrogen; selected recurrences → postcoital/continuous antibiotic prophylaxis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vaginitis: discharge, pruritus, external burning
Urethritis: sexual exposure, discharge, positive gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT
Bladder pain syndrome: chronic symptoms, repeatedly negative cultures

table.title: Initial antibiotics; tailor to culture/resistance
rows: Ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin; initial ceftriaxone if resistance risk
IV ceftriaxone; cefepime/piperacillin-tazobactam if Pseudomonas risk
Avoid nitrofurantoin/fosfomycin: inadequate renal tissue levels

vaginitis.name: Vaginitis
vaginitis.scope: Bacterial vaginosis, Trichomoniasis, Vulvovaginal candidiasis, atrophic vaginitis, genitourinary syndrome of menopause
vaginitis.core: Vaginal discharge or irritation requires distinction among dysbiosis, sexually transmitted protozoal infection, yeast overgrowth, and hypoestrogenic mucosal change.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: BV: new partners, douching; trichomoniasis: sexual exposure
Candida: antibiotics, pregnancy, diabetes, immunosuppression; atrophy: menopause or other hypoestrogenic states

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus, dysuria, dyspareunia; discharge appearance overlaps, so symptoms alone insufficient
★ **Fever, lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness** → evaluate PID rather than isolated vaginitis
Postmenopausal bleeding needs assessment beyond assuming atrophy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: BV: lactobacilli depleted, anaerobes expand; Candida causes inflammatory overgrowth; Trichomonas is sexually transmitted
Low estrogen thins epithelium and reduces lactobacilli → mucosal fragility and elevated vaginal pH

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Vaginal pH, saline/KOH microscopy**, history and examination; NAAT improves infectious diagnosis
BV: ≥3 Amsel findings—typical discharge, pH elevation, clue cells, positive amine odor
★ Suspected trichomoniasis + negative wet mount → **NAAT**, not reassurance
Recurrent/complicated Candida → culture or PCR for species; asymptomatic colonization alone needs no treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **oral metronidazole 7 days in women**; treat partners, abstain until completed/resolved
BV → oral metronidazole 7 days or vaginal metronidazole/clindamycin; treat symptomatic pregnancy
Candida → topical azole or oral fluconazole; **pregnancy: topical azole 7 days**, avoid oral fluconazole
GSM → moisturizers/lubricants, then low-dose vaginal estrogen for persistent symptoms; assess contraindication context
Recurrent BV: ACOG 2025 considers male-partner metronidazole + topical clindamycin; older boards omit

rows.label: Complications
items: BV/trichomoniasis associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and increased STI acquisition
Recurrent symptoms → reassess diagnosis, adherence, reinfection, diabetes or resistant/non-albicans yeast

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **retest women at about 3 months**; condoms, partner management
Avoid douching/irritants; no routine partner treatment for uncomplicated Candida

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervicitis: endocervical mucopus, friability, positive GC/CT NAAT
Contact dermatitis: external irritation after product exposure, no infectious findings

vulvar-dermatoses.name: Vulvar dermatoses
vulvar-dermatoses.scope: Lichen sclerosus, lichen simplex chronicus, lichen planus, punch biopsy, topical high-potency corticosteroids
vulvar-dermatoses.core: Chronic vulvar itching, pain, or architectural change requires morphologic diagnosis and biopsy of suspicious or treatment-resistant lesions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Lichen sclerosus: prepubertal/postmenopausal peaks, autoimmune associations; can occur at any age
Lichen simplex: eczema, irritants, persistent scratching; lichen planus: mucocutaneous inflammatory disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus or burning, dyspareunia, fissures; examine perianal skin, vagina and oral mucosa
★ **Nonhealing ulcer, focal thickening, bleeding or changing pigment** → exclude malignancy
Severe scarring may narrow introitus or obscure normal structures; vaginal involvement narrows differential

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Sclerosus/planus: immune-mediated epithelial injury; simplex: itch-scratch cycle causes lichenification

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Careful vulvar examination; **punch biopsy** if uncertain, atypical, suspicious, or nonresponsive
Erosive lesions: sample active edge with intact epithelium; avoid only ulcer center
Wet mount/KOH or yeast testing when infection suspected; repeated empiric antifungals can delay correct diagnosis
Assess architectural changes and symptom response longitudinally; consider oral/dermatology examination with mucosal disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Sclerosus → **clobetasol ointment**, initial intensive course followed by individualized maintenance
★ Simplex → eliminate trigger and **break scratching cycle** with topical corticosteroid, emollients, nighttime measures
Planus → high-potency topical corticosteroid; erosive vaginal disease may need specialist intravaginal/systemic treatment
Avoid fragranced soaps/wipes and harsh cleansing; bland petrolatum reduces friction and barrier injury
Persistent lesion despite adherence → reassess diagnosis/biopsy rather than indefinitely escalating steroid blindly

rows.label: Complications
items: Sclerosus: vulvar SCC risk and permanent loss of architecture; adequate treatment reduces risk
Erosive planus: adhesions/stenosis; all forms may impair sexual function and quality of life
Excessive unsupervised steroid use → local atrophy; undertreating confirmed sclerosus also causes tissue damage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Regular **surveillance and self-examination** for new focal lesions; continue maintenance when disease active
Avoid irritants, treat coexisting infection/eczema, reduce friction; discuss lubricants and sexual pain

rows.label: Mimics
items: Candidiasis: yeast/hyphae or positive culture, discharge; no progressive scarring
Vulvar Paget disease: persistent eczematous plaque despite usual treatment; diagnostic biopsy

table.title: Morphology
rows: Porcelain-white thin plaques; figure-eight, labial resorption
Thick leathery excoriated plaques; accentuated skin markings
Painful glazed red erosions; lacy white borders

vulvar-dermatoses.evidence: Not checked online; established vulvar dermatology and biopsy-directed management.
